articles.title: PH to get coastal radar, surveillance drones from Japan under P1.7-B security deal
articles.summary: Japan has committed 4.3 billion yen (approximately P1.7 billion) in security assistance to the Philippines, including the provision of a coastal radar system for the Philippine Navy and unmanned…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 9:28pm

Japan has committed 4.3 billion yen (approximately P1.7 billion) in security assistance to the Philippines, including the provision of a coastal radar system for the Philippine Navy and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for the Philippine Air Force.

The agreement was formalized on Monday, November 9, through the signing and exchange of notes between Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Katsuro Kitagawa and Foreign Affairs Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro in Manila.
According to Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the assistance is part of its Fiscal Year 2026 Official Security Assistance (OSA) program.

The project marks the first transfer of defense equipment to the Philippines under Japan's OSA framework, which provides equipment, supplies, and infrastructure assistance to strengthen the security and defense capabilities of partner countries.
Under the agreement, the Philippine Navy will receive a coastal radar system, while the Philippine Air Force will be provided with UAVs for monitoring and surveillance operations.
The assistance is expected to strengthen the Armed Forces of the Philippines' maritime domain awareness and surveillance capabilities, particularly in monitoring strategic maritime areas.

Japan noted that the Philippines occupies a strategically important position along major sea lanes, including the South China Sea and the Luzon Strait, making the country an important partner in maintaining regional security.

The Japanese government also emphasized that the assistance would further strengthen security cooperation between the two countries, protect important maritime routes, and contribute to regional peace and stability.

Manila and Tokyo have continued to deepen their defense and security partnership as both countries work toward advancing a rules-based international order and a Free and Open Indo-Pacific. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: The remarkable story behind the secret Canadian guerilla force you've never heard of

image.caption: Some of the first soldiers of Force 136 during training in India in 1945. The covert Chinese Canadian force fought during the Second World War. (Chinese Canadian Military Museum)

blocks.text: Brent G. Hoy's father, Charles Hoy, didn't talk much about what he did during the Second World War.
It wasn't just that it was difficult. He also was part of a covert Chinese Canadian force, sworn to secrecy.
Force 136, part of Britain's Special Operations Executive, was trained in espionage, guerilla warfare and jungle survival for parachute deployment behind enemy lines in Southeast Asia.
These soldiers wore a Canadian uniform and were prepared to sacrifice their lives, despite being shunned by their country, both in law and daily discrimination.
"Fighting for a country that really didn't want you, but nevertheless having that deep sense to contribute," Hoy said of his father.
That complicated legacy is being spotlighted in a black and white photograph selected by Canada Post for a new stamp, to commemorate the country's military history.

It shows 10 out of about 150 Chinese Canadian soldiers who served the Allied war effort with Force 136 and, after the war was won in 1945, came home to become part of a broader push to change how their community was treated. In 1947, the Chinese Exclusion Act was repealed and the entrenched racism Chinese Canadians experienced began to shift.
It was a double victory, says Catherine Clement, a historian and curator whose work excavates stories of the Chinese Canadian experience.
"Helping the Allies win the war, but also helping the Chinese community to win the right, like equal rights, full rights of citizens of Canada".
Canada Post's new Remembrance Day stamp shows 10 soldiers from Force 136 awaiting repatriation in 1945. Brent G. Hoy's father, Charles Hoy, is in the bottom row, second from the right. (Canada Post)

Between 1885 and 1923, Chinese immigrants who came to Canada had to pay at least $50 to enter. The head tax was later raised to $100, then $500, before all Chinese immigration was banned in July 1923.

From then until 1947, all Chinese people — even those born in Canada — were required to register with the government or risk fines, detainment or deportation. They were segregated within society too, like being prevented from working in some professions or swimming in some public pools.
Operation Oblivion
It was under those laws, designed to exclude or ostracize people on the basis of their Chinese ethnicity, that Hoy's father, at the age of 26, still decided to volunteer in the war effort for Canada.

It was the same story for Rick Wong's father, Hank Wong, the son of a head tax payer and a member of Force 136, also called Operation Oblivion. Hank, who died in 2019, was the last surviving member of the original 13 members of the top secret mission to sabotage supply lines and equipment within Japanese-occupied territory in the Pacific.

Wong says despite first being rejected from the navy, because it was "for white men only," his father eventually joined the Kent Regiment and learned to parachute out of planes and rapidly deploy from moving trucks.

It was in the 1940s, when Japan entered the Second War War and began to quickly invade and occupy large parts of Southeast Asia, that the British realised it needed agents in the region to support local resistance fighters.
Undercover resistance
An undated photo of the first recruits of Force 136 training in Darwin, Australia. (Chinese Canadian Military Museum)
Chinese Canadians were the perfect recruits, from the perspective of Britain's Special Operations Executive, easily blending in with local populations with language skills in English and Cantonese.
Force 136 was born.

Then began intense training in Canada and abroad, including in espionage, wireless operation and jungle survival. Their mission was to gather intelligence, support local resistance fighters and carry out sabotage operations.
They were told to expect extreme heat, insects and disease, alongside the dangers of capture, torture or death.
Members of Force 136 training in Queensland, Australia in 1945. (Chinese Canadian Military Museum)
'A suicide mission'
One recruit, dropped into Borneo, recalled living on crocodile meat, monkeys and wild pigs, in a story highlighted by the Chinese Canadian Military Museum.
"They were told to save your last bullet for yourself, carry cyanide, if you're captured don't reveal any secrets," said Wong.
He says he once asked his father if he was afraid about what was "essentially a suicide mission" while he was awaiting his deployment in Australia.
His father replied, "you gotta do what you gotta do."

Then the Americans dropped the atomic bomb on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, in early August 1945. More than 80,000 people were killed instantly. A few days later, the war ended and so too did Operation Oblivion.
While most of Force 136 sailed back to Canada through England, some men, including Wong's father, were abandoned in Australia.
"They had to work their way back on a freighter in order to get back," said Wong.

When they did get back to Canada, it took another two years until discriminatory laws were repealed. Many see Force 136 and the dismembering of legislation like the Chinese Exclusion Act as inseparably linked.

When those men returned they continued fighting, says Melissa Karmen Lee, the CEO of the Chinese Canadian Museum in Vancouver. It's the only place in Canada, including the War Museum in Ottawa, where the public can see a permanent exhibit on Chinese Canadian soldiers.
"Their faces belong on a Canadian stamp, their stories belong in our history books, and their legacy belongs to every Canadian," Lee said.
Rick Wong, left, and Brent G. Hoy unveil the new Canada Post stamp in Vancouver on Nov. 3. (Spill Studios)
'That's my dad there'

Hoy told an audience at the unveiling of the stamp in Vancouver that he could visualize his father's "broad and knowing closed lip smile of approval" that the contributions of Force 136 would be memorialized in such a way.
His father, who died in 2002, appears in the stamp in the bottom row, second from the right.
Hoy says he was thrilled "beyond words" when he was sent a mock-up of the stamp.
"I thought, hey gee, you know that's my dad there."

While the stamp features only a handful of the faces behind Force 136, Hoy says it marks an acknowledgement of gratitude for the Chinese Canadians that were prepared to sacrifice their lives. None lived long enough to see this commemoration.
"This selfless sense of duty shines a bright light on the fact that we, as a generation after them, are the offspring of our ancestors' courage, persistence, commitment and sacrifice."

articles.title: Sara Duterte’s ‘loose investments’ in Gencorp earn her P2.1-M ‘return of capital’
articles.summary: An article of incorporation presented by the prosecution during the impeachment trial shows the Vice President paid P46,000 in capital stock

blocks.text: An article of incorporation presented by the prosecution during the impeachment trial shows the Vice President paid P46,000 in capital stock

MANILA, Philippines – An in-house corporate counsel of Gencorp Industries Inc. denied that Vice President Sara Duterte has business interests in the company, despite it being listed in her sworn Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs).

On Day 42 of the impeachment trial on Wednesday, November 11, Suzette Balucanag-Punay refuted a portion of the forensic financial report of lawyer Alexander Cabrera, which indicated that Duterte owns a 20% stake in Gencorp and has paid-up capital in the company amounting to P250,000.

Balucanag-Punay also said Duterte is not a stockholder of Gencorp and does not participate in any stockholders’ meetings. She said the Vice President also has no involvement in the board of directors, management, as well as in the decision-making of the company.
“She is not a beneficial owner of Gencorp,” the corporate counsel told the impeachment court.
Balucanag-Punay, however, said Duterte received more than P2.1 million in “return of capital” from Gencorp between 2022 and 2025 from what she described as “loose investment.”
Duterte received return of capital amounting to P337,500 from Gencorp in 2022; P555,750 from May to December 2023; P612,419 in 2024; and P636,700 in 2025.
She, however, did not receive any return of capital from January to April 2023.

“I termed it as a loose investment, your honor. It’s coming from the contributions that the Vice President made for Davao Bounty Times before the actual commencement of the operations of Jollibee Times Square,” said Balucanag-Punay.

According to the witness, Duterte initially invested in Davao Bounty Foods Corporation, a company that attempted to acquire the franchise of a Jollibee branch in Davao. The franchise, however, was not granted, and Duterte’s investments were carried over to the companies that operated the Jollibee Times Square branch, including Gencorp.
Gencorp now operates five Jollibee branches in Davao: Centerpoint Plaza, Davao Gaisano Mall, Abreeza Mall, Times Square Plaza Center, and Bolton.
Balucanag-Punay said Duterte’s investments only covered the Jollibee Times Square branch and not Gencorp. She also said she is unaware of the nature of the investments and their exact amount.
An article of incorporation presented by the prosecution showed Duterte paid capital stock to Davao Bounty amounting to P46,000.
Prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan pressed Balucanag-Punay on Duterte’s possible other investments in Gencorp, citing the ballooning of her investment from P46,000 to P2.14 million.

“I am unaware if there’s any because I cannot verify it from other records,” Balucanag-Punay said, adding she could not confirm how the returns of capital were calculated and if the Vice President still receives income from Gencorp.

Article XII, Section VII of the 1987 Constitution prohibits the president, vice president, and members of the Cabinet from holding any other office or employment during their tenure. They are also barred from “directly or indirectly, practice any other profession, participate in any business, or be financially interested in any contract with, or in any franchise, or special privilege granted by the Government or any subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries.”
Balucanag-Punay’s responses did not sit well with some senator-judges, including Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo, who questioned her credibility.
“You know that you will testify here, so you should have researched. Now, you cannot even present any document that would back up your claims that it was return of investment,” Tulfo said.
Duterte is facing impeachment proceedings under Article II of the articles of impeachment, which involves allegations of unexplained wealth, including allegedly undeclared assets and properties.
As part of the impeachment article, the prosecution challenged Duterte’s inclusion of stock ownership in Gencorp in her 2024-2025 SALN, despite her name’s absence on the company’s corporate records.

In a related development, the defense dropped some of its witnesses, announcing they were dispensing with the testimonies of subpoenaed bank officials — except representatives from Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) — to expedite the proceedings.

“We don’t think there’s a need to waste the time of the court in presenting all of the bank representatives, so we tightened the list and left only the BPI official. It’s in the interest of expediting the proceedings,” defense lawyer Michael Poa said. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte"s defense team will present witnesses who will address any gaps in information team member and spokesperson Michael Poa on Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 9:07pm
Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team at her impeachment trial will present witnesses who will address any gaps in information, team member and spokesperson Michael Poa said on Wednesday.
At the trial, some senator-judges raised concerns about the lack of details in the testimony of GenCorp. Industries and Metro City Chow Foods in-house lawyer Suzette Balucanag-Punay.

Asked about how the defense planned to address these gaps, Poa said that there will be other witnesses to be presented that could answer questions about Duterte’s Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).

“I don’t think there’s a hierarchy of gaps or anything like that but with the questions of the senator-judges, for example, ‘Why is it in the SALN’, ‘Why do the SEC [Securities and Exchange Commission] documents reflect otherwise’, those are the issues we will address with future witnesses,” Poa said in a mix of English and Filipino.

Senate impeachment presiding officer Francis Escudero had grilled Balucanag-Punay over the “loose investment” made by Duterte. Balucanag-Punay admitted that she did not know why Duterte was receiving payments from a fast food branch that the she had supposedly invested in.
Asked about the witness’ lack of knowledge on the matter, Poa said that there was still a limit to how much witnesses knew.

“Mayroon siyang limit sa kanyang testimonya and that’s why we said kung may iba pa tayong mga tanong [There is a limit to her testimony and that’s why we said that if there are other questions], that could be answered by probably another witness… We understand and appreciate the sentiments or perhaps the questions in the minds of the senators, we expected that, and that’s why we’re prepared with another witness to supply that information that they’re probably looking for,” Poa said.
To save time, the defense has already dispensed with bank representative witnesses except for a representative from the Bank of the Philippine Islands, according to Poa.
The spokesperson has yet to divulge the identities of their remaining witnesses from the defense. — BM, GMA News

Russia's chief negotiator at the latest Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi said Wednesday after their conclusion that mutual understanding ‌had been achieved on some issues, but not on others — and that more negotiations would take place.
Flurry of talks, large-scale prisoner swap expected to follow two-day session in Abu Dhabi

Russia's chief negotiator at the latest Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi said Wednesday after their conclusion that mutual understanding ‌had been achieved on some issues, but not on others, and that more negotiations would take place.
In remarks broadcast on Russian state television, Vladimir Medinsky said that a ​new potential future European security framework had been ​a central theme in the two-day talks.

"Together with the American side, we exchanged our views on this; ​on some points we reached a common understanding, ⁠whilst on others we ⁠did not. And this ‌discussion will, of course, continue. The world needs a new, modern, updated security system — one that is fair and does not disadvantage any particular countries," Medinsky said.

Vladimir Medinsky, an aide to Russian President Vladimir Putin, is shown Monday at the trilateral talks between the United States, Russian and Ukrainian delegations, in Abu Dhabi. (Rula Rouhana/Reuters)

He was cool ⁠however on the prospect of European countries joining future talks, and said it was unclear what there was for Russia and the European ‌Union to discuss, given what he said was a lack of proposals from the European side.

"We have not received a single peace initiative or a single concrete peace proposal ​from European countries, so it is unclear what there is to discuss," he said. "When ⁠they come up with some concrete proposals, then we’ll give those proposals ⁠some thought.
"As things stand, I think it would be ⁠useful ⁠for them to learn, for ​example, from the American envoys — in terms of common sense, realism and ​a desire to ⁠achieve peace."
Russia and Ukraine had agreed on a large-scale prisoner swap during the talks, Medinsky added, the latest in a long line of such exchanges. He said the details of that would be made ⁠public soon.
The swap may ​happen in ⁠the ⁠next ‌two to three weeks, Russian state news ⁠agency TASS cited Russian ‌Lt.-Gen. Alexander Zorin as saying.
Zorin said the exchange ⁠would consist of ⁠more ⁠than ​1,000 captives on ​each ⁠side. Previous prisoner swaps have usually been of no more than a few hundred prisoners each.

The talks in the United Arab Emirates have been mediated by Donald Trump's envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who, reflecting the unconventional approach of the White House, did not come to their roles with years of foreign diplomacy experience. Kushner, who is also Trump's son-in-law, said talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi were a "first good step."
Kushner and Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday, then meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin after their trip to Russia, Kushner said Wednesday.

David Arakhamia, a close ally ‌of Zelenskyy, said Wednesday ​there was "good momentum" ​from peace talks in Abu ​Dhabi toward reaching ⁠a ‌solution before the end of the ⁠year. The head ​of ⁠his Zelenskyy's faction in ⁠parliament, ⁠Arakhamia said ⁠the talks ​should be multilateral, ​not ⁠trilateral, adding that Europe should be represented.

Trump has intensified pressure on Kyiv to reach a deal, saying it is time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing." Last week, he said the war was close to being settled in a "big beautiful agreement," but he has frequently predicted breakthroughs that have not materialized.
There has been no sign of major compromises or that new issues are being discussed more than 4½ years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In a photo provided by the Ukrainian Emergency Service, firefighters extinguish a garage fire following a Russian air attack in Kharkiv, Ukraine, on Wednesday. (Ukrainian Emergency Service/The Associated Press)

Russian forces control about one-fifth of Ukraine, but territory is not the only issue at stake. Others include future security guarantees, which both sides want, and Moscow's demands that Ukraine adopt neutral status and not join NATO.
Zelenskyy has repeatedly refused to hand over land that Ukrainian troops have died defending.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said wider security talks should only come after a ceasefire. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has rejected the notion of a truce, saying the Europeans were trying to secure breathing space for Ukraine.
Deadly attacks continue

Russian advances at the front line have slowed this year, but Moscow has been pounding Ukrainian cities and energy sites, while Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian oil refineries and other infrastructure.
Each side said the other had launched attacks overnight, despite the peace talks being under way.

articles.title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient in major milestone towards virus-free status
articles.summary: The country begins a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new cases are recorded.

blocks.text: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free.
It had confirmed its first ever case of Ebola early in October when a Kenyan businessman died within days of arriving in the capital, Nairobi.
He had contracted the virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 5,000 people have died in an ongoing outbreak that began in May. His mother also subsequently died.
Kenya's health minister said 135 identified contacts of the infected patients had also completed their 21 days in isolation.
"Today with the discharge of the last patient we can confirm and tell the world that seven patients have recovered - and all contacts have completed their follow-up monitoring," Aden Duale said.
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) described it as an important achievement in the regional response to the outbreak.
"This is an encouraging moment for Kenya and for Africa. We must sustain surveillance and vigilance until the outbreak is officially declared over," Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya posted on X.
Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October.
All the Kenyan cases were linked to the man who had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda, with health officials reporting no evidence of wider community transmission.
Those who have recovered following treatment included four healthcare workers.
Five patients were discharged on 3 November, followed by a sixth three days later, before the final patient was cleared on Wednesday.

Under World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, 42 days must pass after the last patient tests negative and is discharged, or the last Ebola victim is safely buried, before an outbreak can be declared over.

The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks.
Duale said the government would maintain heightened surveillance at border crossings, airports, health facilities and communities throughout the countdown.
Emergency response teams will remain on alert across the country, while the health authorities will continue monitoring travellers arriving from affected countries.

Kenyans returning from Ebola-affected areas are required to complete electronic health declarations before travelling, undergo screening on arrival and spend 21 days in quarantine under the supervision of health teams.
The minister also urged countries that had imposed travel and visa restrictions to reconsider them - adding that Kenya had no intention of serving as a quarantine centre for another country.
In May, a Kenyan court suspended US plans to open an Ebola quarantine facility for American citizens.
Kenya has maintained that there is no need to restrict domestic travel, trade or public gatherings.
The outbreak has nevertheless disrupted international travel, with some Gulf countries introducing restrictions affecting travellers from Kenya and other African countries.
Saudi Arabia stopped issuing visas to Kenyan nationals in late October, prompting concerns among those seeking employment there.
Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced that it is lifting its suspension on issuing new visas to Ugandan nationals, easing restrictions introduced in June.
But Ugandans will have to spend at least 21 days outside of Uganda before being allowed to travel to the UAE.
The UAE is also allowing certain students, diplomatic passport holders and Ugandan embassy employees to enter under approved health procedures.
Uganda, which shares a long and busy border with DR Congo, was among the countries first affected but declared its own Ebola outbreak over on 27 August.
The current outbreak in DR Congo has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

articles.title: Where Cambodia’s war left minefields, Angelina Jolie made a home
articles.summary: ‘It's not a sacrifice to live a life for others. It's a great joy,’ Angelina Jolie says, reflecting on her adoption of her Cambodian son Maddox and her more than two decades of work with Cambodia

blocks.text: STAR. Actress and humanitarian Angelina Jolie poses at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival.
Sara Komatsu/WikiPortraits
‘It's not a sacrifice to live a life for others. It's a great joy,’ Angelina Jolie says, reflecting on her adoption of her Cambodian son Maddox and her more than two decades of work with Cambodia

items: Angelina Jolie began her deep connection with Cambodia during the filming of 'Lara Croft: Tomb Raider.'
At the ASEAN Inclusive Growth Summit in Manila, Jolie expressed her commitment to preserving Cambodian culture and creating opportunities for its people.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Before a piece of Cambodian land scarred by the Khmer Rouge could be reborn as a home, Angelina Jolie first had to quite literally dig out the dangers of its past.
“The first few years, we were just demining the area, the place that is now my home. We actually found 48 landmines,” she said.

Much of the early work was about clearing explosives and making sure nearby schools and communities were safe and not being threatened by illegal gem mining, poaching, or deforestation operations. Eventually, it evolved into the Maddox Foundation, which now supports communities in Cambodia’s Samlout region.
All this began two and a half decades ago when Jolie came to Cambodia to make a movie.

Speaking at the ASEAN Inclusive Growth Summit in Manila on Wednesday, November 11, Jolie recalled how a trip to Cambodia to film Lara Croft: Tomb Raider became the beginning of a lifelong relationship with the country.
At the time, she knew little about the country beyond its painful history of war, violence, and suffering.
What she found surprised her. Despite everything Cambodians had endured, she encountered people who were warm, generous, and extraordinarily welcoming.
“I couldn’t believe their spirits were so strong after all they had suffered,” Jolie recalled. “There was also just something. You go to certain places, and you just feel at home.”
And Cambodia would eventually become just that — a home.
During a return visit, while volunteering at a school with Cambodian children, Jolie remembered being overcome by an extraordinary feeling.
“I had this thought as clear as day that my son is here and I have to find him,” she said. “And then I met Maddox.”

Maddox was just seven months old when Jolie adopted him from an orphanage in Battambang, northwestern Cambodia, in March 2002. Now 25, Maddox has also followed his mother into filmmaking, including working with her on First They Killed My Father, a film about the country of his roots.

Jolie would go on to purchase a small piece of land near Cambodia’s border with Thailand, in a region once devastated by the Khmer Rouge. She hoped to restore it and create a home for herself and her family.
But Jolie wants to do more.

Alongside her at the summit was Cambodian filmmaker Rithy Panh, who worked with her on her 2017 film First They Killed My Father, a story about a young girl forced to become a child soldier during the Khmer Rouge regime.
Panh, himself a survivor of that terrible period in Cambodia’s history, wanted the story told on the terms of his people.
“Don’t make the film about Cambodia, but with Cambodia,” he said.

And while there was much talk about hope for Cambodia and the good work that has already been done, Panh also offered a sobering reminder of how fragile that future could be, especially for Cambodia’s most vulnerable.
He recalled a family whose children had to travel by boat to attend school. When oil prices rose following the Middle East crisis, the children stopped going. It was simply too expensive.
“When President Trump made war in the Middle East, what happened to the people of Cambodia?” he asked. “What happened to these children?”

That concern for the welfare of ordinary people is what has taken Jolie and Panh’s friendship beyond filmmaking and into a deeper effort to preserve Cambodia’s culture and create opportunities for its people to thrive beyond merely receiving aid.

Jolie also shared plans to bring her creative venture, Atelier Jolie, to Cambodia. Originally based in New York, the initiative provides spaces for artists and craftspeople to connect with each other and international markets.
Through it all, Jolie remains hopeful about what she and the communities around her can continue to build together, because, as she puts it, “We have to.”
“It’s not a sacrifice to live a life for others,” she said. “It’s a great joy.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
articles.summary: Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah is being tried on the charge of "publishing false news" and potentially faces imprisonment.

blocks.text: A criminal court in Cairo has postponed the retrial of the prominent Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, whose case has drawn international condemnation.
Wednesday's opening hearing was adjourned until 18 November after defence lawyers representing the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr requested a new judge.
The UN has warned of "widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities, including the targeting, persecution and harassment of independent journalists".
Attalah told the BBC that a recent crackdown was meant to "send a chilling message" to "the very few newsrooms that are left".
She warned: "Everybody should be careful, everybody should be scared, everybody should be wondering if they are next."
Set up 13 years ago, Mada Masr became Egypt's leading independent news site with Attalah as its editor-in-chief and co-founder.

Last month, another Cairo court convicted her of running a website without a licence - which she said she had tried in vain for years to obtain. She was issued a hefty fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds ($56,000; £42,000) and Mada Masr was ordered to shut down.

After that trial, Attalah found that a court had previously given her a one-year prison sentence, without her knowledge, for "spreading false news" - a charge often used against journalists and dissidents - as well as operating a website without a licence. It was issued in absentia in 2024, even though she was in the country at the time. Attalah is now being retried in that case by the same judge.

Egypt has largely stifled freedom of the press, ranking 169th out of 180 countries for press freedom, according to Reporters Without Borders' 2026 analysis. The group says that at least 26 journalists who were arrested in recent years remain in detention.

While most newspapers and television stations now keep to government lines, Mada Masr remained a rare, independent and investigative news source in Egypt. However, since 2017 the site could only be viewed from outside the country.
It had reported on alleged corruption and human rights abuses, and provided deep coverage of politics and economics, as well as regional upheaval and wars in Libya, Sudan and Gaza.

In her BBC interview on Sunday, Attalah insisted that the factual reporting and professional standards of Mada Masr had an important role to play in Egyptian society, which could benefit the government.

"It's much better if you have a little space left to have it open for professional media organisations who do rigorous reporting, because if we disappear, then you make the space for conspiracies and disinformation," she said.
"People need to know, people need to consume information and you're shooting yourself in the foot if you're killing the newsrooms that do it properly."

In September, six journalists with the independent fact-checking platform, Matsda2sh - constituting its entire newsroom - were arrested in home raids by the Egyptian authorities and held incommunicado for nearly a week.

They have since been charged with joining the Muslim Brotherhood and financing terrorism, and their lawyers report that several were beaten and electrocuted in detention. They say that no evidence has been presented linking them to the Brotherhood.

Egypt's former president Mohammed Morsi – who was backed by the Muslim Brotherhood – was removed from power by the military, led by Abdul Fattah al-Sisi, in July 2013 after widespread protests. Under Sisi, who became president the following year, the Islamist movement was classed as a terrorist organisation, leading to a widespread clampdown.
On Tuesday, a spokesperson for the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Thameen Al-Kheetan, called for the Matsda2sh reporters to be released, with all charges dropped.
He also said the case against Attalah "raises fresh concerns regarding due process and fair trial".
"We call on Egypt to end all forms of harassment of journalists and media outlets, and to respect and fulfil the right to freedom of expression, including the right to information," Al-Kheetan said.

"The steps taken to suppress the continued work of both Matsda2sh and Mada Masr must be overturned. The people of Egypt have a right to read and hear views expressed through these fora on issues of legitimate public concern."
Attalah has suggested the authorities might again be trying to silence independent voices at a time of economic strain in Egypt and regional instability.

It has been widely noted that recent legal action against journalists comes after the US State Department waived human rights conditions on $320m (£240m) in its foreign military funding for Egypt in September. This allowed the funds to be released as part of Washington's annual $1.3bn military aid package.

The BBC asked US Secretary of State Marco Rubio whether he had raised the recent crackdown on independent journalism with Egypt's Foreign Minister, Badr Abdelatty, at their meeting about regional tensions in Paris on Monday.

"We didn't discuss it today," Rubio said. "But… like anything else in foreign policy, there's always a balancing act to further the national interest of the United States. And in the end, Egypt has been a reliable and good defence partner of the United States."
"That doesn't mean you agree with everything another government does," he went on, adding that he was not "opining about their journalists".

articles.title: Hundreds of Italian schools hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax
articles.summary: Emails containing the false warnings were sent to schools in Rome, Naples, Vicenza, Florence, Pisa, Trieste and other Italian cities, officials say.

blocks.text: Some 300 schools across Italy have received bomb threats, according to Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara, who described the incidents as probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk".
Valditara told Italian TV that there was a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in Italy and elsewhere in Europe which had targeted flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.
The emails were sent to schools in Rome, Naples, Vicenza, Florence, Pisa, Trieste and many other Italian cities, and a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution.
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called a meeting of top ministers and intelligence chiefs.
Meloni said the government was monitoring closely the "numerous reports of bomb threats at educational institutions" although checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger".
"These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook.

Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption. Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.
Italian reports said 280 school head teachers had received threats in recent days.
Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, according to reports from a number of regions, and pupils were allowed to return to class.

In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report".

In a separate incident, more than 300 schools in Northern Ireland were sent emails which police said they were treating as a hoax. Messages sent to number of schools in Scotland were also being treated by police as a hoax. It is unclear whether any of the incidents are connected.

articles.title: NPC sounds alarm as 10 gov’t agencies report leaks
articles.summary: The National Privacy Commission reminds government agencies that filing breach notifications does not exempt them from liability after potentially exposing sensitive citizen data

blocks.text: The National Privacy Commission reminds government agencies that filing breach notifications does not exempt them from liability after potentially exposing sensitive citizen data

items: The National Privacy Commission of the Philippines received breach notifications from 10 government agencies regarding potential data leaks, in compliance with the Data Privacy Act.
The Securities and Exchange Commission and Bureau of Internal Revenue reported specific incidents of data breaches, with the SEC attributing its breach to malware and unauthorized access.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The National Privacy Commission (NPC) announced on Tuesday, November 10, that 10 government agencies had submitted breach notifications following reports of potential data leaks.
In a statement released on Tuesday, the NPC confirmed receiving personal data breach notifications from the following offices:

items: Presidential Commission on Good Government
Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)
Department of Labor and Employment, through its Bureau of Local Employment
Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR)
Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation
Department of Justice, through its Office for Alternative Dispute Resolution
Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
Philippine Coast Guard
Department of Trade and Industry
Department of Science and Technology-Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology

blocks.text: NPC spokesperson and Deputy Privacy Commissioner Jose Belarmino II said the notifications comply with Republic Act No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012, and NPC Circular 16-03.

“Each notification received by the NPC is reviewed and assessed by our Compliance and Monitoring Division, which examines the nature and circumstances of the reported incident…. Following its assessment, the Division prepares a report containing its findings and recommendations for submission to the Commission En Banc,” Belarmino explained.
The announcement comes a week after the commission said it was coordinating with government agencies to verify reports of suspected government data leaks.

blocks.caption: NPC probing reports of alleged gov’t data leaks

blocks.text: Under Section 20 of the Data Privacy Act, personal information controllers like government agencies are required to “promptly inform” the NPC and affected individuals if any sensitive personal data has been compromised.

The SEC notified users of its online platforms on Monday, November 9. In an email notice sent to registered users, the commission attributed the leak to “malware infection or unauthorized access by a third-party threat actor” targeting users’ devices.

blocks.caption: DATA LEAK ADVISORY. Screenshots of the email notice sent by the Securities and Exchange Commission informing registered users of a personal data breach. Contributed screenshots

blocks.text: The SEC warned users that exposed records may have included their full names, usernames, email addresses, mobile numbers, birth dates, genders, addresses, and Taxpayer Identification Numbers. But it maintained that “no data was altered, no internal corporate record was involved, and no passwords” were exposed.
According to a statement, the commission detected the breach on November 6 and reported it to the NPC three days later on November 9.

The BIR also issued an advisory on November 9 stating that it was addressing potential breaches in coordination with the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center and the DICT-National Computer Emergency Response Team.
Both the SEC and BIR expressed that they had taken security measures after the cybersecurity breaches.
As of this posting, the other eight government agencies have yet to release official statements about the reported data leaks.
Section 21 of the Data Privacy Act holds personal information controllers accountable for personal information under their custody, including records processed by third parties.
Belarmino emphasized that submitting a breach notification does not exempt government agencies from their responsibility in protecting personal data.

“The NPC expects government agencies to demonstrate accountability not merely through compliance with notification requirements, but through concrete and effective measures to safeguard personal data and prevent similar incidents from recurring,” he said.
The NPC added that it continues to monitor the reported security incidents across several government agencies and urged the public to stay alert against potential security threats. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Sherwin Gatchalian flags GenCorp 'conflict of interest' over Sara Duterte payouts
articles.summary: Senator-judge and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday raised a possible conflict of interest after GenCorp Industries Inc. paid Vice President Sara Duterte P2.14 million as returns of…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 7:58pm

Senator-judge and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday raised a possible conflict of interest after GenCorp Industries Inc. paid Vice President Sara Duterte P2.14 million as supposed returns of capital while the company held several contracts with the Davao City government.

Gatchalian raised the issue during his interpellation of lawyer Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of GenCorp and Metro City Chow Foods Corp., two companies linked to the Vice President, during the 42nd day of Duterte’s impeachment trial.
“Lumalabas ito sa kaha ng GenCorp. Tapos ang GenCorp, sa mga huling hearing, nagbebenta rin po ng pagkain sa Davao LGU (local government unit), 19 contracts between 2022 to 2025,” Gatchalian said.
(This payments came out of GenCorp.’s coffers. GenCorp., as revealed in previous hearings, also sold food to the Davao City government under 19 contracts from 2022 to 2025.)

“Tingin niyo hindi ba ito conflict of interest na ang GenCorp nagbabayad ng investment, loose investment kay Vice President Sara, pero sa kabilang banda, nagbebenta naman siya sa Davao LGU?” he asked.
(Don’t you think this is a conflict of interest, with GenCorp. paying Vice President Sara for her loose investment while also selling food to the Davao City government?)
Duterte’s brother, Sebastian “Baste” Duterte, is the incumbent Davao City mayor. The Vice President also previously served as the city’s mayor.
In response, Punay said the Davao City government contracts were fulfilled by GenCorp.’s Jollibee Bolton branch, the outlet nearest city hall, and not the branch where Duterte had her investment.
She explained that although GenCorp. owns the Bolton branch, Duterte’s "loose investment" was in the Jollibee Times Square branch. Each branch, she added, maintains a separate bank account.
Gatchalian, however, maintained that GenCorp. was still the entity making payments to the Vice President.
“So mukhang conflict of interest… Dahil sa kabilang banda, ‘yung investment binabayaran, ‘yung kita sa investment. Sa kabilang banda naman, nagbebenta ng pagkain sa Davao LGU,” he said.
(So it appears to be a conflict of interest because, on one hand, the returns on the investment are being paid, while on the other, the company is selling food to the Davao City government.)
Punay maintained that there was no conflict of interest.
“To my understanding, there's no conflict of interest because VP Sara is not part of the LGU,” she said.
Gatchalian countered that Duterte and the Davao City mayor are siblings.
Earlier in the hearing, Punay testified that Duterte had a “loose investment” in GenCorp, from which she received P2.14 million in returns of capital from 2022 to 2025.
The amount was significantly lower than the P212 million in alleged returns earlier presented by prosecution witness and financial forensic expert Alex Cabrera.

Duterte’s 2024 and 2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth, which she jointly filed with her husband, Manases Carpio, were earlier presented by the prosecution as evidence of her business interests.
The documents listed GenCorp, formerly known as Times Square Bee Foods Corp. and Great Jolly Times Food, among her business interests.
Baste Duterte previously testified that the Davao City government had awarded P33 million worth of contracts to GenCorp.
He also said he was unaware that his sister had a business interest in the company.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Transport workers in Chile block highways in protest over surging fuel prices
articles.summary: Hundreds of bus and lorry drivers are blocking traffic along major highway routes across the country.

blocks.text: Hundreds of transport workers in Chile have blocked roads and highways across the country in protest over high fuel prices.
Drivers of busses and lorries began protesting on Tuesday, gathering in convoys to halt traffic along major routes.
They are demanding a relief from surging diesel prices, which have been driven up by the war in Iran.
Talks between government officials and protest leaders have so far failed to reach a resolution, with another meeting expected to take place on Wednesday.
The protest is being organised by the ⁠Fuerza del Norte trade union, which represents around 80% of Chile's lorry drivers, and the No+TAG civic protest ​movement.

"There is no point of agreement with the government that could offer any perspective to find solutions for everyone," Andrés Alarcón, a spokesman for No+TAG, said after talks broke down on Tuesday, adding "the strike continues".
Economy Minister Daniel Mas called for further dialogue, but warned "at some point, we will have to clear the highways".
He stressed the protests were impacting economic activity and exports, saying "we need to get the country moving again".
The government of President José Antonio Kast has faced public discontent over fuel prices for months.
The average price of diesel has risen 74% since March, according to industry groups.
Juan Cornejo, the president of the Association of Intercity Bus Owners, which represents 14 mid-sized companies, told AFP that "we've reached our limit".
"We've spent more than a month working with negative numbers," he added.
Lorry driver Claudio Elguezabal, who took part in a protest near the capital, Santiago, on Tuesday morning, said the situation was unsustainable.
"Right now I'm not making any profit. Sometimes you even have to put in your own money to cover the client," AFP quoted the 47-year-old as saying.

articles.title: Donald Trump's ASEAN attendance set for November 17
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit on November 17, joining several other world leaders in Pasay City, Philippines, according to the…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 7:34pm

US President Donald Trump is set to attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit on November 17, joining several other world leaders in Pasay City, Philippines, according to the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Wednesday.
The DFA said that the leaders and delegates from around the world will travel to the Philippines from November 16 to 18, with the opening ceremony of the ASEAN Summit to be held on November 15.
From November 16 to 17, the DFA said that the government will hold Related Summits or the Plus One Summits.

“On 17 November, the President will also convene the 29th ASEAN Plus Three Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, the premier Leaders-led forum for dialogue and cooperation on strategic, political and economic issues of common concern and interest in the region,” the DFA said.

“The President will also lead the Closing Ceremony and the handover of the ASEAN Chairship to Singapore. The day will culminate with the ASEAN-United States Special Summit to be attended by U.S. President Donald J. Trump,” the agency added.

Leaders from other ASEAN nations are also expected to attend, namely Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Lao PDR, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Viet Nam. Myanmar will be represented by its ASEAN Affairs Department Director-General.
There will also be remarks from Brazilian and Canadian leaders, as well as the International Monetary Fund. They are deemed as “Guests of the Chair”.

“As the Philippines brings together ASEAN Leaders and Dialogue Partners from across the region and the wider international community, the country looks forward to engagements that will reinforce the value of dialogue, deepen partnerships, and strengthen collective responses to shared challenges,” the DFA said.
Trump’s attendance has raised concerns among several civil society groups, with many announcing protests to denounce his visit to the Philippines. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Joining lawsuit, Kennedy family members say Trump's arch would be 'denigration' of JFK, RFK plots at Arlington
articles.summary: Nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty are asking a judge to block U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 76-metre structure would cast a…

image.caption: Tourists visit the gravesite of former U.S. president John F. Kennedy at Arlington National Cemetery in Arlington, Va., in a 2013 file photo. (Jewel Samad/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New

Nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty are asking a judge to block U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 76-metre structure would cast a shadow over their relatives' gravesites at Arlington National Cemetery.
Legal filing comes with Trump administration eager to break ground on temporarily blocked project

Nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty asked a judge on Tuesday to block U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 250-foot (76-metre) structure would cast a shadow over their relatives' gravesites at Arlington National Cemetery.

The shadow would "fundamentally alter the experience of visiting the gravesites," the relatives argued. They filed a motion to intervene in two existing lawsuits seeking to block construction of the arch.
U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan last week prohibited the Trump administration from breaking ground on the structure for 14 days.

The nine Kennedy family members who filed suit are children and grandchildren of Robert F. Kennedy and Edward M. Kennedy, brothers of the slain U.S. president John F. Kennedy, both of whom served in the U.S. Senate. They are buried close to the eternal flame that marks JFK's gravesite, a trio of memorials that are a major draw for the millions of people who visit the Arlington cemetery each year.
Sen. Tammy Duckworth, of Illinois, speaks at a demonstration against U.S. President Donald Trump's proposed arch on Oct. 1 in Washington. (Kylie Cooper/Reuters)
Building the arch would be a "permanent denigration" of the gravesites, lawyers for the relatives wrote.
"The Arch would significantly damage the memorial to the Kennedys, as well as the heroes who eternally rest at Arlington National Cemetery," the filing said.

"It is unfortunate to see that some members of the Kennedy family have joined the litigation against the Arch, as the project is intended to honour our heroes who rest in Arlington Cemetery," said White House spokesperson Davis Ingle. "The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation."
Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Trump's health and human services secretary, who has a fractured relationship with many of his relatives, did not join the lawsuit.
LISTEN | Our CBC Washington correspondents look ahead to next Congress session:
Two Blocks from the White House31:02The U.S. midterms are over. Now what?

The arch project is one of several around Washington that the Republican president has undertaken as he alters the capital to his tastes — from renovating one of its storied public golf courses, to threatening to demolish the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. Those projects could soon face intense scrutiny as Democrats will take control of Congress in early January after the results of last week's midterm elections.

The White House last week unveiled a glitzy new website to showcase the arch, which is slated to rise in a mass of gold ornamentation and stately grey granite between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

The family is represented by veteran Washington lawyer Norm Eisen and Democracy Defenders Fund. Eisen and his organization have also filed lawsuits against the Kennedy Center plans and represented a man who successfully fought off prosecution related to an incident at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, after Trump ordered renovations for that Washington, D.C., monument in a no-bid contract.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: Germany news: Only 1/3 of Germans satisfied with state of democracy
articles.summary: A new authoritarianism study has revealed a new low in satisfaction levels with the functioning of German democracy. Meanwhile, the Bundeswehr has banned Chinese-made drones. DW has more.

image.caption: The study also found a high level of chauvinistic and antisemitic tendencies among respondentsImage: James Zabel/Kirchner-Media/IMAGO

blocks.text: November 11, 2026
Satisfaction with democracy in Germany reaches new low — study
Just a third of respondents said they were satisfied with the state of democracy in the Federal Republic of Germany, according to a new report from the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study.

This marked a steep decline from the 42.3% level of satisfaction measured in the last study in 2024 and was the lowest point since the study began in 2002. The level was even lower in the former East German states where only 22.8% expressed satisfaction with German democracy, down from 29.7%.
At the same time, 89.3% of respondents said they agreed with the concept of democracy, however, this also marked the first time this level fell below 90%.
A large share of respondents also expressed chauvinistic and antisemitic views.
In response to the statement "Germany is being dangerously overrun by foreigners," 34.9% were manifestly in agreement, with 24.4% in latent agreement.
At the same time, 15.5% manifestly agreed with the statement "the influence of Jews in Germany is still too great," with 21.7% latently agreeing.
The research was carried out by the Else-Frenkel-Brunswik-Institut at the University of Leipzig. They surveyed 2,500 people between mid-March and the beginning of June this year.

articles.title: Iran classes Argentina navy, air force as 'terrorist organizations'
articles.summary: In a tit-for-tat move, Iran has said it now considers Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organizations." Tehran claimed Buenos Aires is responsible for further consequences.

image.caption: Tehran did not mention Argentina's army in the statement [FILE: Mar 19, 2024]Image: Str/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Iran's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday that it classified Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organizations."

In early April, Argentina designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a "terrorist organization," as US President Donald Trump pressured his allies to do so following the war on Iran.
Tehran's designation came "based on the principle of reciprocity," Iran's ​Foreign ‌Ministry said in a statement.
All the Ayatollah's men — ensuring the regime's survival
"It is ‌evident ​that the responsibility for all consequences arising from this matter will lie with the Argentine government," the ministry added, ​without a mention of Argentina's army.
Iran passed a legislation in 2019 that grants retaliatory measures against states that designate its military as a terrorist group.
Argentina holds Hezbollah responsible for deadly attacks
Argentina said in April that it had taken action against the IRGC because of its support for the Lebanon-based militant group Hezbollah.

blocks.caption: The 1994 bombing attack that destroyed the AMIA building in Buenos Aires left 85 people deadImage: Daniel Luna/dpa/picture-alliance

blocks.text: Buenos Aires holds Hezbollah responsible for the 1994 bombing of the AMIA Jewish community center, which killed 85 people.
IRGC classified as a terrorist group by many countries
IRGC was established at the end of Iran's 1979 Islamic Revolution as an elite armed militia whose role was to protect the then embryonic Shiite clerical regime.
Over the years, it has morphed into a vast economic and political empire. Rather than the elected president, the force answers directly to Iran's supreme leader.
The United States, the European Union, and the United Kingdom, along with other countries, classify the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organization.

items: Summit Media has acquired full ownership of PEP.ph and SPIN.ph, enhancing its digital media portfolio.
PEP.ph, founded in 2006, focuses on Filipino celebrity news and lifestyle content, while SPIN.ph, launched in 2012, covers a wide range of sports topics.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Summit Media has taken full ownership of entertainment and lifestyle news website PEP.ph and sports publication SPIN.ph, the digital media and publishing company announced on Wednesday, November 11.

PEP.ph was founded in 2006 by editor-in-chief Jo-Ann Maglipon. It has since served as a portal into the lives of Filipino celebrities through showbiz news and blind items. It also publishes content on beauty, finance, and other entertainment-adjacent topics.
PEP.ph, which stands for Philippine Entertainment Portal, was jointly launched by Summit Media and GMA in 2007.

Meanwhile, SPIN.ph, which stands for Sports Interactive Network, was launched in 2012 under a joint partnership between Summit Media and GMA. Its coverage spans anything and everything sports — from tennis to esports to leagues like the PBA, PVL, UAAP, and the NCAA, among others. It is helmed by editor-in-chief Eduardo Catacutan Jr.

“These brands have built something that cannot easily be replicated: credibility, audience relationships, and a deep understanding of Filipino popular culture. Our next chapter is about building on those strengths and expanding the ways audiences experience entertainment,” Summit Media president and CEO Howard Go said in a press release.

This comes just after Summit Media formed a partnership with PlayTime Entertainment in the form of a venture called PT Summit. It aims to use technology to distribute content, engage audiences, and come up with new models in the evolving media ecosystem.

“Our focus is on building capabilities that allow established content businesses to evolve, reach audiences in new ways, and explore opportunities that were previously difficult to pursue. This partnership is about creating the foundation for what comes next,” said Crisanto Roy Alcid, president and CEO of PT Summit.

Amid Summit Media’s move to take full ownership of the two publications, PEP.ph and SPIN.ph will still be able to maintain their editorial voices and exercise their own journalistic standards as they operate daily. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: Trump hails ‘exoneration of a Great American Patriot’ as moves against his defense secretary fail for now

blocks.text: Key events

items: 15m agoGOP branded 'sinking ship' as House Republicans block efforts to impeach Hegseth

blocks.text: GOP branded 'sinking ship' as House Republicans block efforts to impeach Hegseth
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Republican representative Thomas Massie compared the GOP with passengers content to go down with the Titanic after colleagues thwarted his effort to impeach defense secretary Pete Hegseth.

The vote came a week after Republicans lost control of the Senate and House of Representatives in their worst midterm election in more than a half century, and underscored how lawmakers remain wary of crossing Donald Trump, who has signaled his continued support for Hegseth.
“They know it’s a sinking ship but committed to stay on board,” Massie, a Republican congressman who lost his primary after breaking with the president, said.

Top Democrats announced their support for the resolution, but Republicans moved to kill it by referring it to the judiciary committee. Their motion succeeded on Tuesday, by a 211-204 vote, largely along party lines. Massie was the sole Republican to oppose the motion, along with all Democrats.
Trump, who was twice impeached, celebrated what he hailed as the “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot” and lashed out at Massie for forcing the vote.
“The Democrats continue to weaponize and abuse the United States of America,” Trump said on Truth Social. “They must be stopped!”

The Pentagon, meanwhile, declared “total victory”. “The referral of these baseless impeachment articles to the House judiciary committee marks total victory for Secretary Hegseth, the Department of War, and the American warfighter,” Sean Parnell, a department spokesperson, wrote in a social media post.
Some 11 Democratic representatives skipped the vote, the Daily Beast reported earlier this morning, causing the articles of impeachment to fail. Among those to miss the vote was Nancy Pelosi.
If eight of ‌them had voted with fellow Democrats the measure could have proceeded.

House Democratic leader Hakeen Jeffries said he would talk to members about whether to mount a new impeachment effort in the next ​Congress in January when the Democrats who triumphed in the midterm take their seats. “We’ll have that conversation at the appropriate time,” he said.

In other developments:

items: Congressman Jim Jordan, a Republican hardliner from Ohio, won the election to become the next House minority leader in Congress. Jordan beat Representative Steve Scalise, the current majority leader, by 106-73 in a closed-door vote to lead Republicans from January. He replaces the current House speaker, Mike Jonson, who said he would not run when the GOP cedes control to Democrats in the new year.

Meanwhile, Republicans in the upper chamber, re-elected John Thune to serve as Senate minority leader in the next Congress. The GOP senator from North Dakota didn’t face a challenger in the closed-door vote, as Democrats prepare for at least a 10-seat majority in the new year.

Nine members of the Kennedy family sued the Trump administration in an effort to block its construction of a 250-foot triumphal arch. The family’s complaint states that the arch, which is planned for near Arlington national cemetery, would obstruct the Kennedy gravesites, the JFK Eternal Flame and the sightlines of the cemetery, “permanently diminishing these memorials.”

articles.title: VP Sara earned profits from GenCorp., says firm's counsel
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte earned profit from her investment in GenCorp. Industries, Inc., a defense witness at the impeachment trial said Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 7:01pm
Vice President Sara Duterte earned profit from her investment in GenCorp. Industries, Inc., a defense witness at the impeachment trial said Wednesday.

Attorney Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of Gencorp Industries, Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corporation, made the testimony when asked by Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros about Punay’s testimony of the Vice President receiving P2.14 million return of capital from from Gencorp Industries, Inc. from 2022 to 2025.

Punay also testified that Duterte has a “loose investment” in GenCorp. because sheinvested in Davao Bounty Times Food Corporation before the actual commencement of operations of Jollibee Times Square branch.
Punay said that the Jollibee Times Square branch eventually opened under the franchise granted to Great Jolly Times Foods Corporation, an entity which eventually became Gencorp Industries, Inc.
“This [P2.14 million] is return of capital. So, kumita nga siya [Duterte],” Hontiveros asked.
“Yes,” Punay replied.
Hontiveros asked if this means that the Vice President has financial interest in GenCorp., to which Punay again answered in the affirmative.
But when asked by Hontiveros if the Vice President receiving this payout violates the Constiution, Punay replied she was not sure.
Hontiveros pressed her, asking if the Constitution clearly prohibits an incumbent Vice President from having direct and indirect participation in any business.
Punay, this time, gave a categorical answer.
“Yes, it is in the Constitution, your honor,” she said.

Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan also raised the point of the Vice President's earning profits from GenCorp., noting that Punay initially said during the direct examination the Duterte had zero business participation with GenCorp.

“During the direct examination, you were certain that the Vice President has no participation in GenCorp., zero participation, no stock holdings, she has no position. And then you mentioned that she actually had a loose investment, and she was receiving benefits from that loose investment,” Pangilinan said.
He said Punay's pronouncement, therefore, is inaccurate, given that by receiving payouts, the Vice President is clearly involved in GenCorp.

“It is not correct to say that there is no participation [on the part of the Vice President] or no role whatsoever. You [Vice President]) participated as a beneficiary,” Pangilinan, a lawyer like Punay, added.

Duterte’s 2024 and 2025 Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) that she jointly filed with her husband, Manases Carpio—presented as evidence of the prosecution—earlier showed that Gencorp Industries Inc., formerly known as Timesquare Bee Foods Corp. and Great Jolly Times Food, is one of her business interests.

The Vice President also listed Gencorp Industries Inc.’s former name, Timesquare Bee Foods Corp., as one of her business interests in her 2022 and 2023 SALNs that the prosecution presented as evidence.

The defense is presenting its evidence against Article 2 which accuses the Vice President of betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution due to amassing P817 million to P1.5 billion of unexplained wealth due to non-declaration of assets and non-divestment in businesses despite a Constitutional ban. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Merchants can scan unified digital PWD cards for verification --NCDA
articles.summary: The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) said that merchants can scan the newly established unified digital ID to verify its authenticity. However, it stressed that a presumption of…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 6:11pm

The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) said that merchants can scan the newly established unified digital ID to verify its authenticity. However, it stressed that a presumption of regularity should still apply to persons with disabilities (PWD).

The NCDA is rolling out its Unified PWD Identification System (UPWDIS), which is a centralized platform to curb fraudulent PWD cards. The Department of Justice had previously raised the alarm on an estimated 6 million fake PWD cards.

“Ang digital ID natin may unique QR Code po. So, iyong QR code po ii-scan lang ng ating mga merchants and then pag-scan didiretso po iyan sa government portal ng DSWD (Department of Social Welfare and Development), and then makikita po na verified iyong ating persons with disabilities. So ganoon lang kabilis po iyong pag-verify niya,” NCDA spokesperson Walter Jason Alava said on the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon public briefing.

(Our digital ID has a unique QR code. So, this QR code can be scanned by merchants, which will go directly to a portal of the DSWD, then we can see the verified persons with disabilities. This makes it fast to verify.)
However, Alvava said that there is a Department of Justice (DOJ) opinion that stated that there should be a presumption of regularity

“Mayroon presumption of regularity kapag nag-present po ang ating mga person with disability ng kanilang identification. So, kailangan po bigyan natin sila ng discounts and then, kung nagdududa tayo ‘di ba na iyong person with disability, doon lang tayo magbi-verify,” the spokesperson said.

(There is a presumption of regularity if a person with disabilities presents identification. So we need to give them the discounts and then if we doubt the person with disability, that is when we verify.)
Alvava said that registration for the new digital ID is still in-person at local government units, as the council was still checking how to enhance an online registration system.
According to a Facebook post from the NCDA, a physical card may be printed upon request.

People with existing PWD cards only need to bring their IDs as long as they are still valid and unexpired. For first-time registrants, those who do not have an apparent disability must bring a certificate of disability from a licensed physician. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: [Be The Good] Let’s not rely on Leni Robredo
articles.summary: When we look to one person, we miss the opportunity to cultivate a wider selection of politicians

blocks.text: She has spoken. The ship has sailed. Those hoping Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo would run for a national post in 2028 got a reality check on Monday, November 9. This whole fixation on Mayor Robredo though also got me thinking of a related issue: the shallow bench for alternative candidates.

When we look to one person, we miss the opportunity to cultivate a wider selection of politicians. Perhaps this decision of Robredo’s is a chance to widen our horizons and look to new faces. More importantly, it should allow us to examine ourselves. Quoting Mahatma Gandhi, should we not become the change we want to see?

I just came from a week in Cape Town, South Africa with Rappler’s scholars to the One Young World 2026 Summit. JJ Agustin, Gybel Agregado, Kit Posadas, John Mauro Manuel, and Jasser Mohammad are examples of young people who are becoming the change they want to see. They live it every day, in their work in youth political participation, agriculture, women empowerment, and data-driven storytelling. At the summit, which gathered 2,000 young people from over 190 countries, we listened to fellow youth leaders tell stories of the hardships they overcame, the challenges they continue to face, and the hope they keep alive for their communities and countries.
One speech at the summit resonated with me – that of Anna Strolenberg, who, at 31 years old, is one of the youngest members of the European Parliament.
Anna was recognized as one of the Politicians of the Year, an award given out at every One Young World Summit.
Like most of us, she used to think politics was a dirty word, “something for men with big egos and bad suits.”
But, when she was 24 years old, she decided to become a politician, not because she thought she’d be good at political maneuverings, but simply because she was fed up with the status quo.

“Many of you told me you have lost trust in politics because politicians are corrupt, or don’t represent you. And I want to tell you this: do not accept it. Go there yourself and make them change,” she said, to resounding applause.

I know many Filipinos don’t trust politics. Most of us are cynical, or have lost hope and have simply checked out. I get it. The headlines scream with reasons to be jaded: the massive flood control corruption, the poor services and facilities, the red tape and incompetence, the grandstanding with nothing to show for it. We rail against these failures of governance all the time. We are adept at outrage. If dissatisfaction with the status quo was a marathon, we would’ve won it a thousand times over.
But Anna said this cannot be enough.

“I have a warning, because our passion for protest doesn’t translate to a passion for politics. Young people have the most to gain, but by not being present, we accept that other people put us last,” she said.

Anna refused to accept this. Not even 30 years old, she set aside her nerves and doubts, and decided to join Volt Europa, a political party. The story of Volt is in itself striking. It was founded by three young people who met while studying at Columbia University and who decided they wanted to create a truly pan-European progressive political party that would push back against the nationalist, right-wing movements gaining ground in the region.
That was in 2017. Today, Volt has over 30,000 members from all over Europe, 400 members elected into office, including five in the European Parliament. Anna is one of those five.

“I know that politics is often a dirty word, but I think it’s up to us to change it. I am proud to say I’m a member of the European Parliament, that I’m changing politics – step by step, but I’m changing it,” said Anna at the One Young World Summit.

All over the world, we are seeing young people stepping out of their comfort zones, and getting some power in return. From France, to Nepal, to Bangladesh, to Serbia, youth-led protests and movements have sparked change, replaced regimes, or at the very least, catalyzed urgent conversations.

In the US, the youth vote played a decisive role in the blue wave that has given back power to the Democrats. Some 66% of voters aged 18 to 29 voted for Democratic candidates for the House of Representatives.

For sure, it is a difficult, even dangerous, road to take back power. In the Philippines, the electoral system is such that massive resources are needed to run for public office. But people with extremely limited resources can change the fate of a nation. South Africa gives us the best example. Nelson Mandela and his fellow freedom fighters against apartheid were facing deadly state force and next to no funding, not to mention a whole ecosystem of discriminatory laws, yet still managed to bring down the repressive system. It came at a great cost. But it was a cost they took on because the dream was worth it.
What dream for the Philippines is worth the cost? What cost are you willing to pay?

You can start by registering to vote in the 2028 elections, if you haven’t yet. Voter registration resumed on Monday, November 10 and will continue until July 30, 2027. You can register to vote at any Comelec office and certain malls, from 8 am to 5 pm. Here’s the directory of Comelec offices nationwide.
